title: Automated Data Quality Monitoring & Anomaly Detection
problem: Modern analytical and machine learning data pipelines suffer from silent data corruption when upstream schemas drift, values violate business domain constraints, or statistical distributions shift unexpectedly. Undetected corrupted data propagates through downstream warehouses and dashboards, producing flawed metrics and erroneous automated business decisions. This project implements an automated, declarative data quality monitoring and anomaly detection engine in Python and DuckDB that validates dataset contracts, checks referential integrity, detects statistical outliers and distribution shifts, and enforces automated blocking gates before pipeline loading.
use_cases: Automated data contract enforcement on daily batch data warehouse ingestion tables
Pre-training data validation for machine learning feature stores preventing corrupt inputs
Continuous schema drift and anomaly detection on third-party API data sync pipelines
hard_parts: Executing complex declarative validation rules across hundreds of thousands of rows within sub-second execution limits
Calculating statistical distribution drift metrics (Wasserstein distance, z-scores) without loading entire datasets into memory
Preventing false positive alerts on legitimate seasonal or high-variance data spikes
Designing fail-fast blocking ingestion gates that halt downstream jobs while outputting actionable failure diagnostics
screener_signals: Declarative YAML contract parser validating column types, nullability, uniqueness, and custom SQL expressions
High-speed analytical validation engine executing inside DuckDB without external database dependencies
Anti-fake verification script injecting dynamic anomalous rows at runtime and asserting automated gate blockage

components.name: Contract Specification Parser
components.purpose: Parses YAML data contract definitions, validating column constraints, rules, and alert thresholds

components.name: DuckDB Validation Engine
components.purpose: Executes vectorized SQL queries evaluating completeness, freshness, uniqueness, and referential checks

components.name: Statistical Anomaly Profiler
components.purpose: Computes historical baseline metrics, z-score outlier bounds, and distribution drift distances

components.name: Pipeline Ingestion Blocking Gate
components.purpose: Evaluates contract results, emits exit codes, and blocks downstream pipeline execution on severe breaches

components.name: Diagnostics & Alert Dispatcher
components.purpose: Generates structured JSON and markdown reports detailing failing row samples and column summaries

architecture.data_flow: Data pipeline triggers the validation CLI passing a dataset path and a YAML contract; the Contract Parser loads rule definitions; DuckDB scans the target Parquet or CSV file directly; vectorized SQL assertions execute in parallel; the Statistical Profiler compares current summary statistics against historical baselines; if all checks pass, the CLI returns exit code 0; if any critical rule fails, the Blocking Gate returns exit code 1 and outputs failing row diagnostics.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: CLI non-zero exit codes halting orchestrator pipelines; strict schema assertions rejecting unmapped or invalidly typed columns.

targets.method: Execution of validation suite across benchmark dataset with 20 intentionally injected data defects
targets.input: Dataset of 200,000 rows containing 20 injected defects (nulls, range violations, regex mismatch, duplicates)
targets.minimum_pass: Detection of 20 of 20 injected defects with 0 false negatives
targets.target: Detection of 20 of 20 injected defects with 0 false negatives
targets.report: Validation execution report listing detected rule breaches and row indexes

targets.method: Wall-clock execution duration to run 15 comprehensive quality checks on tabular dataset
targets.input: 250,000 tabular records stored in Parquet format evaluated with 15 SQL contract rules
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, DuckDB in-memory execution
targets.minimum_pass: Execution completes in < 4.5 seconds across 250,000 rows
targets.target: Execution completes in < 2.2 seconds across 250,000 rows
targets.report: Benchmark execution timing log reporting per-rule execution durations

targets.metric: False Positive Violation Rate on Clean Baseline
targets.method: Validation of verified clean historical baseline dataset against configured quality contract
targets.input: 50,000 verified clean tabular rows matching expected production distributions
targets.minimum_pass: 0 false positive rule violations reported on verified clean dataset
targets.target: 0 false positive rule violations reported on verified clean dataset
targets.report: Validation output summary confirming clean pass

starter_input.spec: YAML data contract specification file and e-commerce transactions dataset in CSV/Parquet format.
starter_input.size: 250,000 transaction rows with 12 columns (transaction_id, customer_id, amount, timestamp, status, country)
starter_input.seeded_cases: Negative transaction amounts, future timestamps, null customer IDs, invalid country codes, and duplicate transaction IDs
starter_input.label_source: Deterministic test fixture generation script injecting exact defect rows at known indices
starter_input.personal_data_policy: Strictly mock synthetic e-commerce transaction data; zero real customer or financial details used

prerequisites: Intermediate Python programming (Pandas, type hints, pytest)
Strong SQL aggregation and analytical querying skills
Familiarity with data pipeline orchestration principles (DAGs, tasks, exit codes)

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU-bound in-process SQL execution)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Python 3.11 and DuckDB installed
environment.fallback_path: In-memory SQLite execution engine without DuckDB if local DuckDB binaries encounter architecture issues

riskiest_component.name: Memory Exhaustion During In-Memory Parquet Scans
riskiest_component.fallback: Leverage DuckDB streaming chunk execution (PRAGMA memory_limit) to bound RAM consumption to 1GB

deliverables: Git repository containing Python data quality framework, CLI executable, and DuckDB runner
Sample declarative YAML contracts defining rules for tabular datasets
Benchmark script verifying defect detection rate and execution speed across 250,000 rows
Screener verification script executing automated validation in under 2 minutes
out_of_scope: Real-time streaming quality validation on Kafka topics
Automated data cleaning and synthetic value imputation
resources: DuckDB SQL documentation and analytical query performance guide
Data Contracts architecture principles and specification guidelines
Scipy statistical distances and drift detection documentation

rubric.action: Run python -m dq_framework check --contract contracts/ecommerce.yaml --data data/dirty_transactions.parquet
rubric.expected_result: Validation engine halts execution, returns exit code 1, and reports all 20 failing rule assertions
rubric.evidence_location: Terminal execution output log and reports/dq_run.json
rubric.pass_criterion: Exit code 1 with exactly 20 distinct failure records reported

rubric.input: Benchmark test running 15 quality checks across 250,000 rows
rubric.expected_result: DuckDB executes all 15 checks in < 4.5 seconds
rubric.pass_criterion: Total execution latency is < 4.5 seconds on local machine

rubric.action: Run python -m dq_framework check --contract contracts/ecommerce.yaml --data data/clean_transactions.parquet
rubric.expected_result: Validation engine confirms all rules pass with zero violations
rubric.pass_criterion: Exit code 0 with 0 rule violations reported

rubric.input: Synthetically skewed dataset with shifted amount distribution
rubric.action: Run python -m dq_framework drift --baseline data/clean.parquet --target data/skewed.parquet
rubric.expected_result: Profiler flags significant distribution drift on amount column
rubric.pass_criterion: Drift detected with calculated distance exceeding configured threshold and warning logged

rubric.input: Dynamic anomalous row with negative order amount (-999.00) injected at runtime by verification script
rubric.expected_result: Engine detects injected negative amount, triggers rule NEGATIVE_AMOUNT_VIOLATION, and blocks ingestion
rubric.evidence_location: Dynamic verification console execution output log
rubric.pass_criterion: Exit code 1 with report pinpointing dynamic row index and rule violation

worksheet.q1: The student builds an automated declarative data quality engine in Python and DuckDB that validates dataset contracts, checks referential integrity, detects statistical drift, and enforces automated pipeline blocking gates.
worksheet.q2: Core path: YAML contract parser, DuckDB SQL validation runner, statistical drift profiler, and blocking ingestion gate (29h). Extended path: Slack/PagerDuty alerts and Great Expectations importer/exporter (+14h).
worksheet.q3: Components: Contract Parser (5h), DuckDB Engine (4h), Drift Profiler (5h), Blocking Gate (4h), Dirty Data Benchmark (4h), Docs & Buffer (3h). Total 25h x 1.15 = 29h.
worksheet.q4: Project types: Data pipeline/ETL/streaming, CLI/tools/libraries. Metrics: Seeded Quality Defect Detection Rate, Dataset Validation Execution Latency, False Positive Rate on Clean Baseline. Rejected: model prediction accuracy.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: executing complex declarative SQL across large files efficiently, distribution drift calculation without memory bloat, tuning outlier thresholds, and fail-fast pipeline gating.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 250,000 transaction rows with 12 columns and 20 injected defects at known row indices. No personal data.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: in-memory SQLite if DuckDB encounters issues.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Memory bloat on large Parquet scans. Fallback: DuckDB PRAGMA memory_limit.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: hardcoded pass/fail reports. Anti-fake check 5 appends a dynamic row with negative order amount at runtime and asserts blocking gate failure.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; synthetic e-commerce transaction data only.
